The signatories warn that AI agents can produce more code and documentation than a person can assess, while unchecked errors can be copied into later work (github.com). A study of local open-weight models found that agents often identified the vulnerable code and formed a correct hypothesis but failed to produce a working input that would trigger the vulnerability (arxiv.org). Separately, Together AI said an AI coding agent committed a repository credential that enabled an unauthorized party to download stored prompt samples. The company said it was continuing to review potentially exposed customer data (together.ai). Trace failures: A case study of 100 support-agent traces recorded 12 failures, including seven cases in which the agent asked for details instead of calling a tool and two involving misapplied policy rules (github.com). Security changes: Together AI said it made zero data retention the default for new accounts, added credential checks to pull requests and changed development rules for AI coding agents (together.ai). Model testing: Researchers tested 12 local model configurations on 10 vulnerability-reproduction tasks. Every configuration handled most of the six easier tasks, while the four harder tasks required the 27-billion-parameter model (arxiv.org). Review standard: The manifesto argues that success should be measured by what users receive and how it helps them, rather than code volume, merged pull requests or the number of agents running (github.com).

title: OpenRouter removes three AI providers after prompts exposed in breaches
description:
OpenRouter, a service that routes customer requests to third-party AI model hosts, removed three providers and revoked Zero Data Retention eligibility for 125 endpoints after researchers at Dragos found prompt data stolen from three inference providers. OpenRouter said it notified potentially affected customers and found no breach of its own systems. The 125 endpoints include precautionary removals, not 125 confirmed breaches.

Dragos seeded about two million prompts with unique links and test credentials from July through November 2026. Researchers found that credentials had been used to probe cloud accounts and that some requests marked for no retention had been copied or forwarded. One test link appeared in a workplace chat in China 24 days after it was sent. Providers can see prompts as they pass through a routing chain, and some requests were copied before a model processed them. OpenRouter said it was checking routing paths and would require assurances and validation before restoring endpoint eligibility.

title: South Korea’s education minister resigns after last-minute AI cheating measures cause confusion
description:
South Korean Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin resigned Sunday after last-minute changes to anti-cheating rules caused confusion before the Nov. 19 national college entrance exam, known as the Suneung. President Lee Jae Myung accepted his resignation about an hour later. The changes followed a Nov. 15 confession by the top scorer on a national tax-accountant exam, who said he used a miniature camera and smartphone to cheat with artificial intelligence.

Authorities responded with device bans, stickers for clothing buttons, Wi-Fi restrictions and surprise emergency phone alerts. The annual exam carries high stakes for university admission and career prospects. Choi faced criticism for both the last-minute rollout and his statement to lawmakers on Nov. 16 that he was not confident he could stop AI-assisted cheating.

Officials identified 111 exam violations involving electronic devices, though not all necessarily involved AI cheating. President Lee tasked Prime Minister Han Seong-sook with overseeing follow-up measures, and the Education Ministry is reviewing cases before releasing scores Dec. 11.

title: COP31 draft sets 2035 electrification goal without clean-power rules
description:
A new COP31 draft sets a collective ambition to raise electricity’s share of global final energy use to 35% by 2035 and expand carbon capture, use and storage to gigatonne scale by that year. The text, drawn up by the Turkish and Australian summit co-presidents in Antalya, does not explicitly call for a transition away from fossil fuels or require the additional electricity to come from renewables. Governments had yet to approve it.

The electrification target concerns energy used across the economy, not a renewable-power quota. The latest draft also drops an earlier version’s direct link to tripling renewable capacity by 2030 and doubling the annual rate of energy-efficiency improvement.

The draft postpones decisions on a 2035 adaptation-finance goal and the timing of future Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) assessments, while noting those reports’ relevance to the 2028 global stocktake. The closing plenary was repeatedly delayed on Sunday as negotiators considered whether to adopt the text.

Adaptation-finance demand: Developing countries sought

title: Rohingya groups demand sanctions as governments weigh Myanmar court ruling
description:
Rohingya organizations and governments are pressing for action after the International Court of Justice, the U.N.’s top court, found Myanmar responsible for genocide against the Rohingya in 2017. A statement endorsed by 64 Rohingya groups urged the U.N. Security Council to enforce the judgment and called for sanctions, arms restrictions and limits on jet-fuel supplies. The groups said any return must be safe and voluntary, with citizenship and equal rights.

Myanmar is in a civil war, and the Arakan Army controls most of Rakhine State, including areas where many Rohingya would return. Myanmar’s government called the ruling unfair and pointed to the court’s 9-6 vote, while Malaysia said it respects the judgment and will engage with the U.N., the Organization of Islamic Cooperation and ASEAN on issues arising from it.

At the United Kingdom’s request, the U.N. Security Council is scheduled to hold closed consultations on the ruling on Nov. 25 and a private meeting on Dec. 7. Whether the council will take enforcement action remains uncertain; China and Russia hold vetoes.

title: El Salvador deploys 2,500 soldiers to Haiti without UN command
description:
Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele sent around 2,500 soldiers to Haiti to search for four aviation technicians who have been missing since October 18 and support operations against gangs. The mission began on October 28 under a bilateral agreement whose terms have not been disclosed; the troops operate outside the chain of command of the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF).

Haitian and Salvadoran forces recaptured Sylvio Cator Stadium, which had been under the control of armed groups, and Salvadoran soldiers established a base there. The Bukele government says its troops will withdraw once they locate the four men, whose whereabouts remain unknown; meanwhile, Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé established a coordination cell on November 9, without publishing details about how it would operate.

title: SEC investigates Nvidia’s accounting practices
description:
The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating Nvidia’s accounting practices, according to people briefed on the inquiry. The investigation is at an early stage and could end without charges. Its precise focus remains unclear, including whether it concerns Nvidia’s geographic revenue reporting or financing arrangements with AI companies and data-center projects.

Nvidia interim chief executive Colette Kress said the company would be more selective about financing deals in the AI industry. The SEC’s enforcement division recently created a financial-reporting and accounting unit. The Justice Department is reviewing Nvidia’s proposed $12.9 billion acquisition of open-source platform Hugging Face as part of a broader antitrust investigation.

title: Bambu Lab at Costco
description:
&&&

Bambu Lab at Costco · A1 Combo bundle · San Diego · November 21, 2026

Bambu Lab at Costco: What the $419.99 A1 Combo Bundle Gets You, and Who Fixes It When It Jams

Costco’s website sells a Bambu Lab A1 Combo bundle. We priced it against Bambu’s own store, read both return policies and Bambu’s warranty fine print, and mapped out who fixes what when it jams.

A 3D printer for sale a few clicks from the bulk paper towels still feels a little strange, but here we are. Costco’s site lists a Bambu Lab A1 Combo bundle, item 2066547, at $419.99: the A1 printer, its AMS lite four-spool feeder, four spools of Bambu’s PLA Basic, and two spare hotends. When we checked on November 21, 2026, it showed out of stock for delivery to a San Diego ZIP code and out of stock in-warehouse at a San Diego location.

So is it a deal? That turns on two things the listing doesn’t spell out: how much filament is on those four spools, and whether Bambu treats a Costco receipt like one from its own store. We repair Bambu printers across San Diego County, so we also cover the part nobody prices in: who fixes it when it jams.

$419.99Costco’s online price for the bundle, item 2066547, on Nov 21.
$359.00Bambu’s US store price for the A1 Combo alone the same day ($399.00 regular).
$9.25What each of the four spools has to be worth for the bundle to beat Bambu’s sale (our arithmetic).
1 yearThe warranty Costco’s listing states. Bambu’s 2-year US term is written for its own store’s buyers.

The short version

  • What you get: an A1 Combo (the A1 plus the AMS lite feeder), four PLA Basic spools, a 0.4 mm hardened steel hotend and a 0.2 mm stainless hotend. Bambu’s own A1 Combo box has 20 g of sample filament and the stock 0.4 mm hotend.
  • Price: at Bambu’s sale price, the printer and the same two hotends cost $382.98. The bundle costs $37.01 more, so the four spools have to be worth $9.25 each. Full 1 kg spools would be; the listing doesn’t give a weight (our arithmetic).
  • Only want the printer? Bambu’s store was $60.99 cheaper on Nov 21. At Bambu’s regular $399.00, the bundle wins before you count the spools.
  • Returns: Costco’s guarantee is the bundle’s strongest card. 3D printers aren’t on Costco’s 90-day electronics list, but the policy says limitations apply, so ask at the membership counter and keep the box.
  • Warranty: plan on 1 year from Bambu, not 2, and ask Bambu to confirm coverage on your serial number with the Costco receipt before anything breaks. Costco wasn’t on Bambu’s US reseller list when we checked.
  • Repairs: inside the warranty, open a Bambu ticket first. Hotends, nozzles, plates and PTFE tubes aren’t covered by anyone’s warranty, and that’s where we come in, along with setup ($159.99 for printers bought elsewhere), out-of-warranty repair and video help.

Five things the listing and the deal threads get wrong

The A1 isn’t enclosed.
Costco’s spec table lists the A1’s features as “Enclosured.” It’s an open-frame printer with a bed that slides front to back, and Bambu’s own FAQ says it doesn’t recommend enclosing the A1. Bambu lists PLA, PETG, TPU and PVA as the A1’s ideal filaments, and the moving bed needs clearance in front and behind.
Its top speed is 500 mm/s, not 550.
The listing gives 550 mm/s. Bambu’s spec page lists a 500 mm/s maximum toolhead speed and 10,000 mm/s² acceleration. Either way, that’s a ceiling, not the speed a typical print runs at.
Bambu’s 2-year US warranty is written for its own store.
Bambu moved US and Canada printers to two years in August. Its policy page, updated Sept 22, 2026, says that extension applies to products bought through Bambu Store US and Bambu Store CA. Costco’s listing says 1 year. Bambu also says only receipts from Bambu or “distributors authorized by Bambu Lab” count for warranty, and Costco wasn’t among the 48 US and Canada sellers on Bambu’s authorized reseller list on Nov 21. Ask Bambu to confirm your coverage in writing.
The $50 gift card is gone, and so is $50.
A July deal post listed the bundle at $469.99 with a $50 Bambu.com gift card. On Nov 21, Costco’s page showed $419.99 and no gift card in the box list. It’s the same math either way: $469.99 minus $50 of store credit is $419.99.
Skip the support email printed on the listing.
The address on Costco’s page has a typo in the domain. Bambu says warranty cases go through its support page, so start there.

What’s in the Costco box, and what’s in Bambu’s

Costco’s bundle is built on the same A1 Combo Bambu sells: the A1, a bed-slinger with a 256 mm cube of build space, plus the AMS lite, the open four-spool feeder that switches colors for you. The difference is what comes with it.

Item Costco bundle Bambu US store A1 Combo
Printer and feeder A1 and AMS lite A1 and AMS lite
Filament Four PLA Basic spools; the listing doesn’t give a weight 20 g of sample filament, random color
Hotends The A1’s pre-installed 0.4 mm stainless hotend, plus spare 0.4 mm hardened steel and 0.2 mm stainless hotends The pre-installed 0.4 mm stainless hotend
Gift card Listed in July; not in the box list on Nov 21 None
Price on Nov 21 $419.99 $359.00 sale, $399.00 regular
Shipping UPS Ground included Free in the 48 contiguous states

The spare hotends are the useful part. Bambu’s hotend page says its carbon-fiber PLA and PETG run with a low risk of clogging in a 0.4 mm hardened steel nozzle, and warns that filament filled with carbon fiber, glass fiber or metal is prone to clog a 0.2 mm nozzle. So the 0.2 mm hotend is for fine detail in plain filament, and the hardened one is for Bambu’s carbon-fiber PLA and PETG. When a swap is the fix, our A1 hotend guide walks through it.

The price math, two ways

Prices move every few days in late November, so treat these as a snapshot from Nov 21. All of it is our arithmetic on prices we read that day.

Line Price Where it comes from
Costco bundle $419.99 costco.com, item 2066547
A1 Combo at Bambu’s US store $359.00 Sale price; $399.00 regular
0.4 mm hardened steel A1 hotend $11.99 Bambu US store
0.2 mm stainless A1 hotend $11.99 Bambu US store
Printer plus the same two hotends $382.98 Our arithmetic
Left for the four spools $37.01 ($9.25 each) Our arithmetic
PLA Basic 1 kg refill at Bambu $14.99 list; $9.74 at 10+ rolls Bambu US store; refills come without a spool

Read it two ways. If you only want the printer, Bambu’s store was $60.99 cheaper on Nov 21, and Bambu’s 30-day return window and 2-year US warranty come with a store purchase. If you’d buy filament and a hardened steel hotend anyway, the bundle comes out ahead as long as each spool is worth more than $9.25. Four full 1 kg rolls would be worth $59.96 at Bambu’s refill list price and $38.96 at its 10-roll price, both above the $37.01 gap (our arithmetic).

Against Bambu’s regular $399.00, the bundle is already $2.99 cheaper before you count the spools. The catch is the weight: Costco’s page says four PLA Basic filaments and stops there. If they turn out to be small sample spools, the sale price at Bambu wins. The label on each spool will tell you; a kitchen scale will too.

Costco isn’t the only shelf with an A1 on it. Bambu’s reseller list includes Best Buy and Micro Center, and our budget multicolor roundup compares the A1 Combo with its rivals under $500. If multicolor is the point, read our purge waste guide too: every color change burns some filament, and it adds up.

Returns: Costco’s strongest card

Costco’s satisfaction guarantee promises a refund on merchandise you’re not happy with, with a short list of exceptions and no general time limit written into it. The exception that matters here is electronics, which get a 90-day window: televisions, projectors, major appliances, computers, touchscreen tablets, smart wearables, cameras, drones, camcorders, MP3 players and cell phones. 3D printers aren’t on that list.

The policy also says “Limitations apply” and points members to the membership counter. We read it as the general guarantee covering a printer, and we wouldn’t bet a purchase on that reading. We’re not lawyers. Ask at the counter before day 90 and keep the box. We read the policy the same way for the Creality K2 bundle Costco sells.

Online orders can go back to any Costco warehouse, and Costco says there are more than 800 of them, or you can start the return on costco.com. Bambu’s own return window is 30 days from delivery for its store’s buyers, and its policy says products bought from a reseller follow the reseller’s return and replacement rules. For a Costco unit, the return counter is the first stop for anything wrong out of the box.

What the counter can’t do is fix it. Costco’s Technical and Warranty Services offers free support for TVs, computers, tablets, cameras, appliances, home theater gear and printers, and nothing on that page mentions 3D printers. Call and ask, but expect to troubleshoot an A1 with Bambu’s support or with a local shop.

Warranty: what Bambu covers, and for how long

Bambu’s policy page gives a warranty term for every listed part of the A1 and the AMS lite. We drew it as a rack in the figure above: 34 parts at the full term, 4 at three months, and 14 with no warranty at all. That’s our count of the entries on Bambu’s two lists, so a part listed on both counts twice; filament and Maker’s Supply items are left out.

Part group Examples from Bambu’s list Bambu’s term First call
Main printer parts Mainboard, AC and TH boards, motors, belts, heatbed unit, touch screen, camera, fans 24 months* Bambu ticket
AMS lite main parts Mainboard, housing, feeder motor, filament hub, stand 24 months* Bambu ticket
Three-month parts Extruder unit (not its gears or sensor), AMS lite feeder unit, rotary spool holder, microSD card 3 months Bambu ticket, then us
No warranty Hotend with nozzle, heater, thermistor and sock; extruder gears; build plates; PTFE tubes; filament cutter; nozzle wiper; AMS lite funnels and spool claws None You, or us

*24 months is the term on Bambu’s US page, and its policy ties that term to Bambu Store US purchases. Costco’s listing says 1 year.

No warranty doesn’t mean no help. Bambu says it will replace consumables that fail from a manufacturing defect while the printer itself is in warranty, at its discretion. Wear is on you.

Bambu’s claim rules matter if you want a local repair. It wants a ticket through its support page first, with the receipt and photos, video or logs of the problem. It asks owners not to repair damage themselves without its guidance, and it says the warranty becomes invalid if an unauthorized service center works on the printer without its approval. That’s why, inside the warranty, we’ll ask you to open the ticket before we open the printer. If Bambu sends a part, ask on the ticket whether a local tech can install it, and we’ll do it once they say yes. Our support-ticket guide covers what to do when a ticket stalls.

Two more notes. Bambu says its terms don’t take away rights you have under state law, and California has its own warranty rules; we’re not lawyers. And if you’ve read about the A1’s 2024 recall over its heatbed cable, Bambu says A1 printers sold after January 30, 2024 already have the fixes, and Costco’s listing describes the reinforced cable.

What breaks on an A1 Combo, and who fixes it

Here’s how common A1 Combo problems line up with Bambu’s parts list, and what the parts cost on Bambu’s US store.

Problem Usual suspects Part and price Who handles it
Clog, thin or gappy lines Heat creep, damp or dusty filament, filled filament in the 0.2 mm nozzle A1 hotend: $9.99 (0.4 mm stainless) or $11.99 (0.4 mm hardened or 0.2 mm stainless) You can swap a hotend; there’s no warranty on hotends. We clear clogs on visits.
A blob of plastic around the hotend A print that lets go of the plate while the nozzle keeps extruding Heating assembly $19.99, silicone sock $2.99 (Bambu US store, Oct 22) Us, once it’s past the sock
AMS lite won’t feed or keeps retrying A tangled or cracked spool, a worn PTFE tube, the feeder unit PTFE tubes: no warranty. Feeder unit: 3 months Bambu in the first 3 months, then us
Prints won’t stick Fingerprints or wear on the plate, damp filament Build plates: no warranty You, with our plate guide
Layer shifts, grinding, a dead screen or board Belts, motors, the mainboard, the heatbed unit 24-month parts on Bambu’s list Bambu ticket first; us after the warranty

The details live in our guides: clearing a clogged Bambu, the blob of death, AMS feed problems, build plates that hold and when to swap an A1 hotend.

Your first week with a Costco A1 Combo

Do these in order. The first three cost nothing and save the most trouble later.

1Keep the box and every bit of foam

Costco’s return counter and Bambu’s warranty shipping both go easier with the original packaging.

Bambu’s policy says original packaging gives the best protection in transit, and that poor packing can mean extra repair charges or denied coverage for shipping damage. Don’t flatten anything until you know the printer is a keeper.

2Photograph the serial number and save the Costco order

Bambu asks for the receipt and evidence with every claim, so get both on file on day one.

Photograph the serial label and the box label, and save the costco.com order email as a PDF. If something fails in month eleven, you won’t be hunting for them.

3Ask Bambu to confirm your warranty

Open a ticket on Bambu’s support page with the Costco receipt and serial number, and ask what coverage applies.

Costco’s listing says one year, and Bambu’s 2-year US term is written for its own store. A written answer now beats an argument later. Save the reply with the receipt.

4Give the moving bed room

The A1’s bed slides front to back, so set it on a sturdy surface with clearance in front and behind.

A wobbly table shows up as ripples in prints. Our guide to 3D printer tables covers stands, load ratings and circuits.

5Update the firmware and bind the printer

Connect it to Bambu Handy or Bambu Studio and install the current firmware before the first real print.

Bambu sells region-specific printers and says one from the wrong region may not bind to an account or use cloud features. The Costco model number, PF002-A+SA005-US-COS, reads as a US unit; that’s our reading of the number, not Bambu’s.

6Run the calibrations and print one color first

Let the A1 run its full calibration, then print a single-color test before you load the AMS lite.

Bambu says the A1 calibrates its Z offset, bed level, vibration and nozzle pressure for every job. One clean single-color print tells you the printer is fine before color changes add variables.

7Load the AMS lite and keep the spares dry

Load the four spools, check that no PTFE tube is kinked, and seal up the spools you aren’t using.

The AMS lite is open to the room. Near the coast, marine-layer mornings mean damp air, and damp PLA strings and clogs. Keep spares in a sealed bin with desiccant.

8Label the spare hotends and learn the swap

Mark the 0.4 mm hardened steel and 0.2 mm stainless hotends and practice a swap while nothing is wrong.

Use the hardened steel hotend for carbon-fiber PLA or PETG and the 0.2 mm one for detail work in plain PLA or PETG. Put the stock hotend back for everyday printing.

Where Dreaming3D fits

We’re an independent repair shop in Carmel Valley, and where you bought the printer doesn’t matter to us. Here’s what we do for Costco buyers:

  • Setup: $159.99 per printer bought elsewhere, Costco included. We place it, calibrate it and run the first prints with you.
  • Repair: in person across San Diego County, $159.99 per printer, parts extra. Los Angeles by appointment; we confirm the date and price when you text.
  • Inside the warranty: we’ll ask you to open a Bambu ticket before we open the printer, and help you put together the photos, video and logs Bambu asks for.
  • Video help: live over Zoom or FaceTime, anywhere.
  • After Bambu’s warranty: our Lifetime Warranty plan is $24.99 a month for one printer, parts and labor, while the plan is active.
  • Printing instead: FDM at $7 a machine-hour and resin at $9, plus material, if you’d rather not own a printer at all.

What we don’t do: we don’t print metal, flight hardware, firearm components, load-bearing or safety-critical parts, or medical devices that touch patients.

A San Diego footnote: Costco’s own history says its first location opened in 1976, as Price Club, in a converted airplane hangar on Morena Boulevard. Bambu has no store of its own in San Diego that we know of (our Bambu retail post tracks where it’s opening), so for now a warehouse club is as close as Bambu retail gets here.

Common questions

Is the Costco Bambu Lab A1 Combo bundle a good deal?

It can be. On Nov 21 the bundle was $419.99, and the A1 Combo plus the same two hotends cost $382.98 on Bambu’s US store at its sale price. The four spools have to be worth $9.25 each to close the gap, which full 1 kg spools would be. If you only want the printer, Bambu’s store was cheaper. That’s our arithmetic on prices that change often.

What comes in the Costco Bambu Lab A1 Combo bundle?

Costco’s listing for item 2066547 lists the A1 printer with the AMS lite feeder, four PLA Basic spools, a 0.4 mm hardened steel hotend and a 0.2 mm stainless hotend. It doesn’t give the spools’ weight. A July version also included a $50 Bambu.com gift card; the Nov 21 box list didn’t.

Does a Costco A1 Combo get Bambu’s 2-year warranty?

Don’t count on it. Bambu’s policy page says the 2-year US and Canada extension applies to products bought through Bambu Store US and Bambu Store CA, and Costco’s listing says 1 year. Ask Bambu to confirm the coverage on your serial number with the Costco receipt.

Is Costco an authorized Bambu Lab reseller?

Costco wasn’t on Bambu’s US and Canada authorized reseller list when we checked on Nov 21. Bambu says only receipts from Bambu or distributors it authorizes are valid for warranty. The model number ends in -US-COS, which suggests a bundle packed for Costco, but that’s our inference. Ask Bambu before you rely on the warranty.

Can I return a 3D printer to Costco after 90 days?

Costco’s 90-day limit covers a named list of electronics, and 3D printers aren’t on it, so the general satisfaction guarantee appears to apply. The policy also says limitations apply. That’s our reading, not Costco’s answer, and we’re not lawyers. Ask at the membership counter and keep the box.

Is the Bambu Lab A1 enclosed?

No. Costco’s spec table says it is, but the A1 is an open-frame printer with a moving bed, and Bambu’s FAQ says it doesn’t recommend enclosing it. Bambu lists PLA, PETG, TPU and PVA as the A1’s ideal filaments.

Will Costco’s tech support help with a 3D printer?

Costco’s Technical and Warranty Services page lists free support for TVs, computers, tablets, cameras, appliances, home theater gear and printers, and doesn’t mention 3D printers. Call and ask, but expect to work through Bambu’s support or a local repair shop for A1 problems.

Will a local repair shop void my Bambu warranty?

It can, under Bambu’s terms. Its policy says the warranty becomes invalid if an unauthorized service center works on the printer without Bambu’s approval, and it asks owners to open a ticket before repairing anything. Inside the warranty, open the ticket first and get approval in writing. Outside it, any shop can work on it.

What isn’t covered by the warranty on an A1 Combo?

Bambu lists no warranty on the hotend and its parts, the extruder gears, build plates, PTFE tubes, the filament cutter, the nozzle wiper, and the AMS lite’s funnels and spool claws. The extruder unit and the AMS lite feeder unit get 3 months. Bambu says it may replace consumables that fail from a manufacturing defect while the printer is in warranty.

Do you fix Costco-bought Bambu printers in San Diego?

Yes, and where you bought it doesn’t matter. In-person repair across San Diego County is $159.99 per printer plus parts, setup for printers bought elsewhere is $159.99, Los Angeles is by appointment, and we help anywhere over Zoom or FaceTime. Inside Bambu’s warranty, we’ll ask you to open a Bambu ticket first.

Bought the Costco A1 Combo? We’ll set it up or fix it.

Text us a photo of the problem, or of the box if it’s still sealed. We’ll set it up, calibrate it and run the first prints with you, or come fix it, anywhere in San Diego County. Inside Bambu’s warranty, we’ll help you file the ticket first.

Book a visit

Or text 858-342-6984, email dreaming3dprinting@gmail.com, or message @dreaming3dprinting.

Setup is $159.99 per printer bought elsewhere; in-person repair is $159.99 per printer, parts extra. Los Angeles by appointment. We don’t print metal, flight hardware, firearm components, load-bearing or safety-critical parts, or patient-contact medical devices.

Sources

We read the Costco listing, Costco’s return policy and support pages, and Bambu’s warranty policy, reseller list and US store pages in a browser on Nov 21, 2026. Prices change often in late November. The A1 heating assembly and sock prices are from Oct 22. The July bundle price and gift card come from a deal post, not from Costco.

title: Canada wins China pork tariff relief, but offal remains taxed
description:
Canada secured tariff relief for some agricultural exports to China during Prime Minister Mark Carney’s visit for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, including the removal of a tariff on pork products. Pork offal remains excluded from the relief. The agreement also extends relief for some other products but is not a free-trade deal.

China is one of the largest markets for Canadian pork byproducts and among the few that buy them. The 25% tariff had made Canadian pork uncompetitive there. Federal Agriculture Minister Heath Macdonald and parliamentary secretary Cody Blois accompanied Carney on the trip. The agreement does not guarantee tariff relief beyond the current extensions.

title: Windows Phone 7 – Emulator Automation
description:
Hi Folks,

In this next blog post we’ll review how to automate the Windows Phone 7 Emulator and what are some real-world usages this technique.

This blog post is the second blog post in a series of unrelated advanced Windows Phone 7 blog posts.
The previous blog post in this series is “Windows Phone 7 – Unlocked ROMs”.

 

Why is Windows Phone 7 Automation Important?

Currently, the Windows Phone 7 Emulator can only launch developer packages (XAPs) from inside Visual Studio 2010.
Meaning, if we’ve got a XAP we can’t get the emulator to load it without Visual Studio.

As we’ve seen in a previous blog post the emulator can be launched and even installed on machines that do not have Visual Studio. More on that here.
Let’s consider that in order to load XAPs into the Emulator we currently have to use Visual Studio. 

The problem is – How do we load XAPs into WP7 Emulators and Devices without using Visual Studio?

So how does our Build Server run nightly tests? Or how do our customers see our applications?

Customers and Build servers don't have Visual Studio 2010 installed.

So, how can we deploy XAPs to an emulator running on these machines?

 

Quit your Jibber-Jabber, show me how to automate the WP7 emulator!

Let’s create a new solution with a Console Application and a Windows Phone 7 Project.

We’ll use the ConsoleApplication as our automation harness that can run on any computer with the .Net framework.
The WindowsPhone Application is the application whose deployment we’ll automate.

 

The CoreCon 10 WP7 API

The secret sauce for WP7 Automation is the CoreCon API.
These CoreCon DLLs have been in deep hibernation since 2007 when they last got a major upgrade.
For WP7 Tools the CoreCon API has been updated and are used by Visual Studio 2010 when deploying applications to WP7 devices and emulators.

Let’s add a reference to Microsoft.SmartDevice.Connectivity.dll from the CoreCon API.
On a x64 developer box, the DLL can be found at: C:\Program Files (x86)\Common Files\microsoft shared\Phone Tools\CoreCon\10.0\Bin\Microsoft.Smartdevice.Connectivity.dll 

 

 

Now that we have the CoreCon DLL reference in place, we can start automating WP7.

Here’s the User Experience we’re aiming for in this demo:

We’ll have to build the following workflow:

     

We’ll start off by getting an instance of the WP7 CoreCon SDK instance to work with:

// Get CoreCon WP7 SDK

DatastoreManager dsmgrObj = new DatastoreManager(1033);

 

Platform WP7SDK = dsmgrObj.GetPlatforms().Single(p => p.Name == "New Windows Mobile 7 SDK");

 

Next up we’ll have to get a reference to either a WP7 physical device or a WP7 Emulator.
This demo will use the emulator, but if we set “useEmulator = false” this demo will try and connect to a physical WP7 device.

// Get Emulator / Device

bool useEmulator = true;

Device WP7Device = null;

if (useEmulator)

    WP7Device = WP7SDK.GetDevices().Single(d => d.Name == "Windows Phone 7 Emulator");

else

    WP7Device = WP7SDK.GetDevices().Single(d => d.Name == "Windows Phone 7 Device");

Now we’ll launch the WP7 Emulator/Device.
Note that the default WP7 Emulator Image is the one we’ll launch into, and in a previous blog post I’ve explained how to use the Unlocked ROM as the default ROM.

// Connect to WP7 Emulator / Device

Console.WriteLine("Connecting to Windows Phone 7 Emulator/Device...");

WP7Device.Connect();

Console.WriteLine("Windows Phone 7 Emulator/Device Connected...");

Next, we’ll have to check if our application is already installed, and if it is – we’ll uninstall it.
Since the the UpdateApplication Method in the current CoreCon API doesn’t work, this is our best bet on easily updating installed apps.

In order to Install or Uninstall our application, we’ll need it’s Application Product Identifier (GUID).
We can get the application GUID from the Properties/WMAppManifest.xml file.

 

We’ll write the code to check if an application is installed, and if it is – we’ll uninstall it.

Guid appID = new Guid("{5e75bba1-fbf6-463c-94ac-fa4a78f8fd12}");

RemoteApplication app;

if (WP7Device.IsApplicationInstalled(appID))

{

    Console.WriteLine("Uninstalling sample XAP to Windows Phone 7 Emulator/Device...");

 

    app = WP7Device.GetApplication(appID);

    app.Uninstall();

 

    Console.WriteLine("Sample XAP Uninstalled from Windows Phone 7 Emulator/Device...");

}

At this point, we’ll install our XAP.
In order to do that, we’ll need 3 pieces of information:
1. The location of our XAP.
2. The Application GUID.
3. The location of the application icon.

// Install XAP

Console.WriteLine("Installing sample XAP to Windows Phone 7 Emulator/Device...");

 

app = WP7Device.InstallApplication(

    appID,

    appID,

    "NormalApp",

    @"D:\visual studio 2010\Projects\ConsoleApplication1\WindowsPhoneApplication1\ApplicationIcon.png",

    @"D:\visual studio 2010\Projects\ConsoleApplication1\WindowsPhoneApplication1\Bin\Debug\WindowsPhoneApplication1.xap");

 

Console.WriteLine("Sample XAP installed to Windows Phone 7 Emulator...");

The last step is to actually launch our application.

// Launch Application

Console.WriteLine("Launching sample app on Windows Phone 7 Emulator...");

app.Launch();

Console.WriteLine("Launched sample app on Windows Phone 7 Emulator...");

 

We’re done. And indeed when we run our sample application the app runs as expected:

 

So What is WP7 Automation good for?

There’s a lot of good use cases: Automating Unit tests, Loading Nightly builds into the emulator and even letting customers use the WP7 Emulator.
There’s really a plethora of reasons and situations WP7 Automation can prove useful in and it’s up to you to figure it out for your projects.

For instance in Vertigo, we’re using the WP7 Automation harness to run the WP7 Emulator on multi-touch laptops that our customers have.
So Vertigo’s customers, as part of an iterative process, get access to our current build without having to install or use Visual Studio 2010.

 

Access to Isolated Storage

One use-case in particular interests me, which is automating running all unit tests in the project after a Continuous Integration nightly build.

We can pretty much do all of the work to automate WP7 tests using WP7 Automation we’ve seen so far, but how do we get results into application? Or get instructions in?

The easiest method I can think off is communicate through cold storage – read & write files into Isolated Storage.

We’ll start off by writing a file into our WP7 Application IsoStore.
Remember that this code executes in the WP7 Emulator/Device.

public MainPage()

{

    InitializeComponent();

 

    SupportedOrientations = SupportedPageOrientation.Portrait | SupportedPageOrientation.Landscape;

 

    using (var isoStore = IsolatedStorageFile.GetUserStoreForApplication())

    using (var sw = new StreamWriter(isoStore.OpenFile("Foo.txt", FileMode.OpenOrCreate, FileAccess.Write)))

    {

        sw.Write("Hello WP7! (Written from WP7 IsoStore, read by Console Harness!)");

    }

}

Basically, We’ve written a Foo.txt file into our IsoStore and added some text into it.

Next, we would have used the RemoteIsolatedStorage class and get access to the emulator IsoStore, but that has not been enabled yet in CoreCon10.

We would have used RemoteApplication.GetIsolatedStorage() but that has not been implemented yet.

We’ll use a FileDeployer class instead.
There’s some reflection magic associated with getting a copy of a FileDeployer class that can be used for our application.

Thread.Sleep(10000);

//app.GetIsolatedStore(); <-- Throws NotImplementedException

object ConManServer = WP7Device.GetType().GetField("mConmanServer", BindingFlags.NonPublic | BindingFlags.Instance).GetValue(WP7Device);

FileDeployer f = (FileDeployer)typeof(FileDeployer).GetConstructors(BindingFlags.Instance | BindingFlags.NonPublic)[0].Invoke(new object[] { ConManServer });

Next, we’ll copy the Foo.txt file from the application isolated storage into our local binary folder and read it into the console:

f.ReceiveFile(@"\Applications\Data\" + appID + @"\data\isolatedstore\Foo.txt", @"\Foo.txt");

 

Console.WriteLine("\t" + File.ReadAllText(@"foo.txt"));

 

When we run this sample we can see the text written from IsoStore showing up on our console.

And we’re done, we’ve esteblished a two-way communication channel between WP7 Emulator/Device and Managed .net code.  

 

Console WP7 Automation Harness Source Code

Here’s the source code we’ve built in this project:

// Get CoreCon WP7 SDK

DatastoreManager dsmgrObj = new DatastoreManager(1033);

 

Platform WP7SDK = dsmgrObj.GetPlatforms().Single(p => p.Name == "New Windows Mobile 7 SDK");

 

// Get Emulator / Device

bool useEmulator = true;

Device WP7Device = null;

if (useEmulator)

    WP7Device = WP7SDK.GetDevices().Single(d => d.Name == "Windows Phone 7 Emulator");

else

    WP7Device = WP7SDK.GetDevices().Single(d => d.Name == "Windows Phone 7 Device");

 

// Connect to WP7 Emulator / Device

Console.WriteLine("Connecting to Windows Phone 7 Emulator/Device...");

WP7Device.Connect();

Console.WriteLine("Windows Phone 7 Emulator/Device Connected...");

 

 

Guid appID = new Guid("{5e75bba1-fbf6-463c-94ac-fa4a78f8fd12}");

RemoteApplication app;

if (WP7Device.IsApplicationInstalled(appID))

{

    Console.WriteLine("Uninstalling sample XAP to Windows Phone 7 Emulator/Device...");

 

    app = WP7Device.GetApplication(appID);

    app.Uninstall();

 

    Console.WriteLine("Sample XAP Uninstalled from Windows Phone 7 Emulator/Device...");

}

 

// Install XAP

Console.WriteLine("Installing sample XAP to Windows Phone 7 Emulator/Device...");

 

app = WP7Device.InstallApplication(

    appID,

    appID,

    "NormalApp",

    @"D:\visual studio 2010\Projects\ConsoleApplication1\WindowsPhoneApplication1\ApplicationIcon.png",

    @"D:\visual studio 2010\Projects\ConsoleApplication1\WindowsPhoneApplication1\Bin\Debug\WindowsPhoneApplication1.xap");

 

Console.WriteLine("Sample XAP installed to Windows Phone 7 Emulator...");

 

// Launch Application

Console.WriteLine("Launching sample app on Windows Phone 7 Emulator...");

app.Launch();

Console.WriteLine("Launched sample app on Windows Phone 7 Emulator...");

 

Console.WriteLine("Reading Foo.txt Isolated Storage file:");

 

Thread.Sleep(10000);

//app.GetIsolatedStore(); <-- Throws NotImplementedException

object ConManServer = WP7Device.GetType().GetField("mConmanServer", BindingFlags.NonPublic | BindingFlags.Instance).GetValue(WP7Device);

FileDeployer f = (FileDeployer)typeof(FileDeployer).GetConstructors(BindingFlags.Instance | BindingFlags.NonPublic)[0].Invoke(new object[] { ConManServer });

f.ReceiveFile(@"\Applications\Data\" + appID + @"\data\isolatedstore\Foo.txt", @"\Foo.txt");

 

Console.WriteLine("\t" + File.ReadAllText(@"foo.txt"));

 

Console.ReadLine();

 

Fin

In this blog post we’ve talked about why Automating the WP7 Emulator and Device deployment process is important and how to go about doing that.
Hopefully now you know how to automate WP7 XAP Deployment.

In the next blog post in this series we’ll talk about setting up a Continuous Integration build for WP7.

 

Leave a Comment

Are there any other use cases for WP7 Automation?
Are you planning on using this technique somewhere?
Was this a good blog post? Sound off in the comments.

 

Sincerely,

-- Justin Angel

title: European-Japanese BepiColombo enters Mercury orbit ahead of two-probe science mission
description:
BepiColombo, a joint mission of the European Space Agency and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency, entered orbit around Mercury on Nov. 21, completing an eight-year journey and becoming the second mission to orbit the planet. The two orbiters remain attached; they are scheduled to separate on Dec. 9–10 and take up different polar orbits, with science operations due to begin in April 2027.

The mission will use the European Mercury Planetary Orbiter and Japan’s Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, called Mio, to study Mercury from separate vantage points. Their instruments are designed to examine the planet’s surface and interior, its magnetic field and the thin gas envelope around it, including how the magnetic field interacts with the solar wind.

Controllers in Germany confirmed the spacecraft’s capture several hours after a series of braking thruster firings, with the spacecraft about 152 million kilometers away. A propulsion-system problem delayed BepiColombo’s arrival from December 2025. Its nominal science mission is planned to last one Earth year, with an extension through 2029.

excerpt: BepiColombo, a joint mission of the European Space Agency and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency, entered orbit around Mercury on Nov. 21, completing an eight-year journey and becoming the second mission to orbit the planet (apnews.com, eos.org, mainichi.jp). The two orbiters remain attached; they are scheduled to separate on Dec. 9–10 and take up different polar orbits, with science operations due to begin in April 2027 (space.com, eos.org). The mission will use the European Mercury Planetary Orbiter and Japan’s Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, called Mio, to study Mercury from separate vantage points. Their instruments are designed to examine the planet’s surface and interior, its magnetic field and the thin gas envelope around it, including how the magnetic field interacts with the solar wind (eos.org, apnews.com). Controllers in Germany confirmed the spacecraft’s capture several hours after a series of braking thruster firings, with the spacecraft about 152 million kilometers away (apnews.com). A propulsion-system problem delayed BepiColombo’s arrival from December 2025. Its nominal science mission is planned to last one Earth year, with an extension through 2029 (eos.org). Orbital paths: Mio is headed for a highly elliptical polar orbit, while the European orbiter will use a less elliptical polar orbit (space.com). Long route: The spacecraft made one Earth, two Venus and six Mercury flybys to shed speed; the looping trajectory covered more than 10 billion kilometers (apnews.com, space.com). Energy challenge: Reaching Mercury is harder than reaching Pluto because a spacecraft must shed enough momentum to match Mercury’s path around the Sun (eos.org). Mission cost: The joint mission is valued at about $2 billion, or 1.7 billion euros (apnews.com, eos.org).
kite_context:
Perspective: Daniel Schmid, research-group leader at the Austrian Academy of Sciences’ Space Research Institute, said measurements of the strength and direction of Mercury’s magnetic field could help explain why the planet has a global field (orf.at). (ORF)
Quote: "What makes this mission really unique is that for the first time in space exploration, we are bringing two spacecraft to the vicinity of the planet, and we are going to put them in orbit around this mysterious body." (Santa Martinez, European Space Agency mission manager for BepiColombo, Eos)
Timeline: 21 November 2026: BepiColombo entered Mercury orbit after braking thruster firings (apnews.com, space.com).
Timeline: 9 December 2026: The European and Japanese orbiters are scheduled to separate (eos.org, space.com).
Timeline: 10 March 2027: The European orbiter is scheduled to reach its nominal science orbit (space.com, sapo.pt).
Timeline: April 2027: The mission’s science operations are scheduled to begin (eos.org, mainichi.jp).
Background: NASA’s Mariner 10 flew past Mercury in the 1970s. NASA’s MESSENGER was the only spacecraft to orbit the planet before BepiColombo, from 2011 until it ran out of fuel and struck the planet in 2015 (apnews.com, eos.org).

title: Lebanon’s Aoun demands Israeli withdrawal, Hezbollah disarmament and end to Iranian influence
description:
Lebanese President Joseph Aoun said Israel’s continued presence in southern Lebanon and Iranian influence over decisions made outside state authority prevent Lebanon from achieving full sovereignty. In a speech on Nov. 21, the eve of Lebanon’s 83rd Independence Day, he demanded that Israel withdraw, stop its attacks and return Lebanese detainees, while urging the Iran-backed armed group Hezbollah to hand over its weapons.

Aoun said the issues were linked and his government would pursue their resolution simultaneously. His address focused on Hezbollah, whose weapons have long exceeded the Lebanese army’s arsenal. The group has said it needs them to resist Israel.

A June agreement reached with U.S. mediation calls for Hezbollah to disarm, Israel to withdraw from southern Lebanese territory and the Lebanese army to deploy there. Implementation has stalled: Hezbollah has refused to surrender its weapons, and Israel continues to strike in Lebanon.

title: DietPi 10.9 adds support for five new single-board computers
description:
The DietPi project has released version 10.9 of its lightweight, Debian-based Linux distribution, adding images for five single-board computers: the Odroid C5 and Orange Pi 4A, Zero 4, 6 and 6 Plus. The Orange Pi 4A currently runs its processor cores at a fixed 768 MHz because of a kernel scheduling limitation; a proposed fix is under review.

The release also adds four applications, including Podman and Paperless-ngx, and introduces a Raspberry Pi fan-control utility. It improves Raspberry Pi temperature and voltage warnings and network reconnection. It also drops Readarr and Mono from the software catalog and disables installation support for Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr and Jackett on ARMv6 devices.

title: Earthquake in Peru leaves one dead, 16 injured and 853 affected
description:
The latest report on the magnitude 6.7 earthquake that struck central Peru on Friday put the toll at one dead, 16 injured, 853 people left homeless and another 529 affected. The deceased was a 45-year-old man who had been admitted to Hermilio Valdizán Medrano Regional Hospital in Huánuco; authorities did not specify the cause of his death.

The report counted 152 uninhabitable homes and 156 damaged ones, as well as damage to six schools, 22 health facilities, four churches, three community centers and about 300 meters of roads. Huánuco, Pasco and Junín sustained the most damage; Lima and Callao were also affected.

Authorities deployed medical personnel, ambulances, emergency response teams and technical crews, and coordinated humanitarian aid with local governments. In Huánuco, they sent machinery to clear roads blocked by rocks. Damage assessments and repairs to restore electricity are ongoing. The Geophysical Institute of Peru reported two subsequent earthquakes in Junín, with no new damage confirmed.

title: Tesla begins FSD v15 rollout with new driving display and safety claims
description:
Tesla has begun sending its Full Self-Driving (Supervised) v15 software to early-access owners, adding a live, photorealistic visualization called Tesla Reality View and claiming a 25-fold improvement in handling safety-critical situations. The update also targets sign recognition, potholes, road debris, standing water and speed control near schools and in bad weather. Tesla says the supervised system can slow for detected speed cameras and adds a mode for cars carrying bike racks.

Reality View renders the surroundings from a virtual camera above the car and displays planned turns. Tesla says it lets drivers see and control what FSD intends to do. The company attributes the claimed safety improvement to an upgraded vision encoder trained on millions of internet videos, but has not published the underlying intervention rate, making the multiplier difficult to assess independently. Tesla chief executive Elon Musk said the wider release is planned for December with Tesla’s 2026 Holiday Update. Tesla has not identified which vehicles will receive the first general-release builds.

title: Finland restricts Gulf traffic as Baltic neighbors join ship rescue
description:
Finland took charge of maritime rescue and pollution-control operations after the Russian cargo ship Sparta II caught fire in the Gulf of Finland and drifted into Finnish waters on Saturday. Finnish officials said Ukraine was likely behind the drone strike; Kyiv had not commented. Authorities temporarily restricted air and sea traffic in the eastern gulf, while the Border Guard said the incident posed no danger to other shipping and reported no environmental damage.

Estonia sent a navy vessel to assist with firefighting and pollution response, and Swedish combat aircraft operating under Finnish command helped safeguard Finnish and NATO territory. A Russian rescue vessel also joined the operation, and Finland said it planned to allow the damaged ship to be towed back to Russian waters.

Hours after the strike, Finland reported that a Russian helicopter had entered its airspace by as much as 4.1 kilometers; Defence Minister Antti Häkkänen said it might have been involved in rescue or surveillance. The ship is linked to a Russian company providing services to the Defence Ministry, but Finnish officials said its cargo had not been confirmed and could include military material.

title: Former federal minister Navdeep Bains wins Ontario Liberal leadership
description:
Former federal industry minister Navdeep Bains won the Ontario Liberal leadership on Saturday, beating Toronto-area member of provincial parliament Lee Fairclough by 50.3% to 49.7% on the third ballot. Bains, who has no seat in the provincial legislature, said he intends to run for one but did not say where or when. He ruled out asking a sitting Liberal MPP to resign for him.

Bains takes charge of a party with 14 seats, behind the governing Progressive Conservatives’ 79 and the New Democrats’ 27. The Liberals have lost three straight provincial elections since Ontario Premier Doug Ford’s party first took office in 2018, and the next election may not come until 2030. Bains campaigned on jobs, economic growth and affordability, while his critics have pointed to his ties to former Prime Minister Justin Trudeau.

title: Bayer Roundup settlement leaves glyphosate debate over farm use unresolved
description:
A Missouri court’s approval of Bayer’s settlement over claims involving its Roundup herbicide does not alter Brazilian registrations for glyphosate products. U.S. farmers use glyphosate to control weeds after herbicide-tolerant soybeans and corn emerge, while Brazilian growers use it for weed control, including before planting in no-till systems. The judge approved a deal worth up to $7.25 billion on Nov. 20 to resolve claims by people who attribute non-Hodgkin lymphoma to exposure; Bayer denies the herbicide causes cancer.

Brazil’s health regulator retained the active ingredient after a reassessment, with risk-mitigation measures. In Europe, Italian farm group Coldiretti urged the European Union to stop imports of Canadian wheat dried with glyphosate, arguing that the practice is prohibited in Italy and the EU and disadvantages local growers.

Alternatives: Coldiretti called for investment in alternatives such as pelargonic acid (agricolae.eu). Regulatory divide: The International Agency for Research on Cancer classified glyphosate as probably carcinogenic in 2015, while the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency says its earlier assessment found no health concern when products are used according to label directions (comprerural.com, wwaytv3.com).

title: African health summit adopts declaration setting 2027 accountability steps
description:
The second Dakhla Global Summit, a meeting on African health and social protection, closed in Morocco on Nov. 21 with participants from 30 countries adopting a declaration on access to care and stronger health systems. The declaration calls for vaccination, organized cancer screening, continuous care, local production of medicines and vaccines, and expanded health-worker training.

The summit’s follow-up plan calls for a first progress report at the 2027 meeting, which is also due to focus on equitable access to care, medicines and vaccines, as well as health data and artificial intelligence.

excerpt: The second Dakhla Global Summit, a meeting on African health and social protection, closed in Morocco on Nov. 21 with participants from 30 countries adopting a declaration on access to care and stronger health systems (anp.ne, maliactu.net). Workforce shortage: The declaration cites an Africa CDC estimate that the continent needs 6.1 million additional health workers by 2030 and calls for sustained funding for training and better working conditions (anp.ne). Investment index: The Health Investment Index will use public international data to link spending with health outcomes, family protection and workforce training. An independent scientific committee will oversee the calculations, which a third party will audit (anp.ne, maliactu.net). Cancer prevention: Burkina Faso cancer researcher Abdou Zouré said HPV type 35 circulates in West Africa but is not covered by any current vaccine. He urged stronger African research and access to future vaccines adapted to regional strains (anp.ne).

title: Haitian operation leaves 54 suspected gang members dead in two days
description:
Haiti's National Police reported that 20 suspected members of armed gangs were killed on Friday, November 20, in Martissant, south of Port-au-Prince, following the deaths of 34 others in the same area on Thursday. The operation used armored vehicles and drones and received support from the Vectus Global task force, a private military company that provides services to the Haitian government.

More than 2,000 Salvadoran soldiers sent by President Nayib Bukele are taking part in the deployment. Three Salvadoran soldiers were killed and another was injured in an explosion while handling explosives at a camp; the contingent is also searching for four soldiers who have been missing since an ambush on October 18. Police say they are seeking to reclaim areas controlled by the gangs.

title: New operator and successor cloud firm widen Nvidia chip-smuggling probe
description:
Li Ming, a 52-year-old Chinese businessman, was a central operator in a network suspected of routing restricted Nvidia AI chips to China, with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang serving as its public face, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the operation. Singapore charged Li in February 2025 with fraud over claims that servers he bought would be used by his Singapore company; the indictment did not name Megaspeed.

The reporting also describes a successor venture, NovaGate Cloud, formed in 2025 by people linked to Megaspeed. NovaGate says it operates data centers using Nvidia’s latest Blackwell chips. Shipping records reviewed by the Journal show at least $300 million in Nvidia-equipped hardware imports through a Malaysian affiliate in the first five months of 2026.

A separate investigation linked companies associated with Alice Huang’s family and associates to about $3.6 billion in Chinese state funding, while noting that it remains unclear whether China’s military used the computing capacity. Former Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before House committees behind closed doors on Dec. 1; a Senate office requested public testimony for Dec. 3.

title: Suspected tainted liquor kills 16 in Manipur, 600 hospitalized
description:
At least 16 people have died and about 600 have been hospitalized after drinking suspected adulterated liquor in Manipur’s Chandel district, state officials said. Twelve patients were in intensive care. Police arrested six people as investigators traced the liquor to Sugnu in neighboring Kakching district.

The precise cause of the deaths and whether the liquor contained methanol remain unconfirmed pending medical findings and laboratory tests. Patients have been treated at hospitals in Imphal and the affected districts. Officials sent medical teams to Chandel and urged residents to avoid liquor from questionable sources.

Manipur has formed a four-member inquiry committee to examine the liquor’s origin and composition, medical and forensic evidence, and possible regulatory failures. The panel must report within one month. Police and excise teams have also been directed to inspect sales and production sites, seize illegal liquor and collect samples for testing.

title: Pentagon restricts US-Canada defense ties in classified memo
description:
U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth issued a classified directive restricting military cooperation with Canada. Republican Sen. Mike Rounds said it limits informal and social contact between the countries’ military personnel. The Washington Post reported that the memo circulated last week but said it had not seen the document. The directive’s full scope remains unclear.

The Pentagon says the guidance refocuses engagement on U.S. defense priorities and will not affect military intelligence sharing, the North American Aerospace Defense Command (NORAD) or cooperation through the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO). Canadian Defence Minister David McGuinty said he had not seen the memo and had observed no change in military cooperation.

President Donald Trump has imposed tariffs on Canadian goods, criticized Canada’s defense spending and repeatedly suggested that Canada become a U.S. state. The Pentagon paused a longstanding bilateral defense forum in May, while Canada says it has reached NATO’s 2% spending target and plans to increase defense spending to 5% of gross domestic product by 2035.

title: Montreal police make first arrests in force misconduct probe
description:
The first criminal arrests in a Montreal police misconduct investigation have prompted civil-rights advocates to call for accountability and wider scrutiny. One said the case could set a precedent for holding officers responsible. Allegations involving a second station, downtown Station 21, include mistreatment of unhoused people and a claim that an officer urinated on someone while on duty.

Quebec prosecutors charged former Montreal police officers Vincent Routhier and Zachary Belzil with assault and breach of trust; Belzil also faces a criminal-harassment charge. Both were released on promises to appear, and no court date had been set. The force’s union is challenging the administrative dismissals of seven officers, and Chief Fady Dagher has said they could be reinstated if those challenges succeed. Related criminal investigations continue under the supervision of an independent observer appointed by Quebec’s public security ministry.

title: Polish farmers warn shrinking margins are reshaping livestock and supply chains
description:
Polish farmers and agriculture officials warn that falling profitability, retailer leverage and changing farm structures are putting producers under pressure. They are calling for closer cooperation, stronger oversight and longer-term contracts. A Nov. 25 forum in Poznań will cover farm costs, competitiveness and food security.

In pig production, speakers cited shrinking herds, reliance on imported piglets and African swine fever restrictions. Proposed responses include coordinating producers and developing domestic quality and breeding programs. Supply-chain participants discussed contract-based partnerships, while a deputy agriculture minister called for stronger market monitoring.

title: Small farms pursue saffron, seed processing and direct vegetable sales
description:
Four farm profiles from Poland and Romania show how producers earn income from agriculture. title: US panel says China aided Pakistan to constrain India's rise
description:
The U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission said in its 2026 report, released Nov. 18, that China backed Pakistan during the May 2025 India-Pakistan fighting after India launched Operation Sindoor. The commission said Beijing showed it could strengthen Islamabad without entering combat, complicating Indian military planning and heightening concern about a two-front threat.

The report describes that support as part of broader military, economic and maritime pressure intended to constrain India’s power. It says Pakistan used advanced Chinese-supplied weapons. Chinese state media later aired an engineer’s account confirming that Chinese personnel provided technical support in Pakistan during the conflict. The commission urged Washington to move beyond periodic exercises to sustained maritime and intelligence coordination with New Delhi, while noting that India’s strategic autonomy means closer ties will not guarantee alignment with U.S. objectives.

Maritime activity: The report cited Chinese naval, surveillance and research vessels operating near India and key sea lanes, including survey ships near India’s exclusive economic zone and the Bay of Bengal during the 2025 tensions (news18.com, timesnownews.com). Cyber operations: The report said hackers attempted large-scale distributed denial-of-service attacks on Indian government, telecom and digital services during the conflict, while the commission said it could not independently attribute the attacks (hindustantimes.com, news18.com). title: Battlefield use of AI weapons grows as Geneva talks leave rules unsettled
description:
AI-enabled weapons are in use in conflicts in Ukraine, Sudan and the Middle East, while campaigners say armed drones that can independently select and strike targets have appeared in limited cases. The International Committee of the Red Cross says commanders must remain responsible for the lawful use of force.

At U.N.-backed talks in Geneva, 128 countries agreed to develop an international instrument on lethal autonomous weapons over the next two years, but left open whether it would be legally binding. Around 100 countries had sought binding rules; the United States, Russia and Israel opposed that push, and the consensus-based forum allowed any member to block stronger language.

The process is expected to examine which systems should be prohibited and which could be regulated. Government experts are to recommend the instrument’s form, including whether it should be binding. The International Committee of the Red Cross says commanders must remain responsible for the lawful use of force, including when weapons act with little or no human oversight.
